decisions.reason: The Hero V remains the unchanged source geometry; the client requests that the lowercase v preserve more of its existing right-arm reach.
The lowercase-v reach change does not alter the accent derivation requirement. The separate accent decision in the same message is already represented by its own same-message MODIFY.
The source changes the subtle reach of the lowercase v's right arm, not the shared terminal cut, ending treatment, or cross-glyph terminal evaluation rule.
A refinement to the lowercase v's right-arm reach does not change the deferred architectural construction requirements for the E and L letterforms.
Preserving a subtle right-arm extension does not change the second V's established smaller, subordinate prominence relative to the Hero V.
The geometric reach refinement has no necessary effect on the deferred champagne material treatment.
The client does not change spacing or the unified-reading goal; any later kerning adjustment would require a separate design decision.
The source does not modify the obligation to explain design intentions with review rounds. Its construction-diagram request concerns the separate É accent derivation.
